result.title: Small Data in Long-Term Environmental Vision: Annotation Noise, Gamification, and Label-Budget Scaling
result.comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to the LFSD-CV Workshop at ACCV 2026
result.summary: Long-running environmental camera networks produce abundant images but few reliable annotations. Using FujiView, a network of webcams around Mount Fuji, we study three linked questions: whether gamification affects annotation participation and agreement, how annotators disagree on ordinal visibility labels, and how label budget affects downstream classification. Across seven nonrandomized sessions with 22 labelers, gamification showed a more promising pattern for sustained participation than for labeling speed or agreement. In the closest remote-session comparison, the session recorded as gamified had longer active labeling time, while throughput and reference agreement remained similar. Annotation disagreement was substantial at fine granularity: crowd votes matched the single-annotator reference on 49.1% of exact visibility classes, versus 90.2% after grouping them into Good/Poor. In five-replicate label-budget experiments, models using 25% of the available label pool achieved held-out exact accuracy only 2.8 percentage points below the full-pool model on average. Together, these findings highlight the importance of designing reliable annotation targets, evaluating engagement mechanisms without assuming causal benefits, and using empirical scaling curves to plan labeling effort.

AI.brief_summary: 基于富士山周边网络摄像头（FujiView），研究游戏化对标注参与度的影响、标注者在有序能见度标签上的分歧，以及标签预算对下游分类精度的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作是可穿戴/环境监测场景下的众包标注与数据规模研究，未涉及内部表征、latent 推理状态、证据筛选或停止决策；标注成本与噪声问题过于通用，未提供可核查的 LVR 方法线索。
